title: Emergent model threat matrix and enterprise adoption triggers
creator: Aisha Cardenas
description:
Objective: Produce a prioritized 'threat matrix' that maps emergent open model features and vendor motions to concrete enterprise adoption triggers (SLA needs, on-prem/KMS requirements, quantization parity) and to Redwood product levers (Dedicated capacity, Private deployment, kernel/quantization recommendations).

Background: Over the last 2 quarters we observed multiple open-model entrants that close key gaps (smaller-context efficiency, improved INT8 quantization, and better function-calling ergonomics). Sales and Solutions report customers asking whether new models mean they can migrate away from Redwood-hosted endpoints. We need a defensible, hypothesis-driven framework to convert market signals into prioritized product responses and procurement triggers.

Scope:
- Scan and score ~18 emergent model variants across 6 enterprise-relevant axes (latency parity, quantization support, private deployability, license/governance risk, tool-calling fidelity, prompt/behaviour drift).
- Run a lightweight benchmarking harness (representative RAG and chat workloads) to measure latency and token-cost deltas vs our hosted endpoints for 3 representative enterprise workloads.
- Conduct 6–8 buyer interviews (platform leads / infra / security) to validate which feature gaps actually move procurement decisions.
- Produce a one-page operational matrix mapping signal severity to product actions (e.g., canary rollout of quantized variant, accelerate private deployment integration, pricing adjustments, new compatibility flag).

Deliverables:
1) Threat matrix spreadsheet with normalized scores and explanation of scoring rubric.
2) Benchmark summary (latency/token cost, sequence-length sensitivity, quantization quality diff).
3) Customer interview notes and decision heuristics.
4) Roadmap decision memo with recommended short/medium product levers and conditional procurement triggers.

Out-of-scope: Deep model re-training, negotiating third-party vendor contracts, or building a production fallback for every model tested.

Success metrics: Clear tradeoff table that the sales+solutions team can use to answer customer migration questions within 48 hours; prioritized list of 3 product actions with estimated engineering effort and ROI ranking.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Completed threat matrix with scores and rationales for >= 12 models; 2) Benchmark summary with median latency and per-token cost deltas for 3 workloads; 3) 6 validated buyer interviews with synthesized decision heuristics; 4) Decision memo with 3 prioritized product actions and estimated eng effort and ROI; 5) Shareable one-page summary for Sales/SEs.
notes: Trade-offs considered: increasing emphasis on private/VPC feature parity reduces short-term hosted revenue but defends churn risk for regulated customers. Quantization recommendations require kernel work (estimate medium effort) vs. recommending a dedicated quantized model variant as a stop-gap. We must balance observable cost delta vs. perceived vendor lock-in. Legal team flagged two models with ambiguous license terms — treat as high risk until clarified.
